g-aml.desc: Spot the red flags before the money moves.
g-aml.title: AML Sprint

questions.q: A customer deposits LKR 950,000 in cash every day this week — always just under the reporting threshold. What is this pattern called?
questions.explain: Splitting cash into amounts below the LKR 1 million reporting threshold to dodge Cash Transaction Reports is structuring. Escalate it for a possible STR.

questions.q: Cash transactions of at least how much must be reported to the FIU as a Cash Transaction Report?
questions.explain: Under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, cash transactions of LKR 1 million or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) are reported to the FIU.

questions.q: It's fine to tell a customer we've filed a Suspicious Transaction Report about them, as long as we're polite about it.
questions.explain: Never. Alerting a customer about an STR is 'tipping off' — an offence. Keep reports strictly confidential.

questions.q: In customer due diligence, what does PEP stand for?
questions.explain: A PEP holds (or held) a prominent public role. They and their close associates need enhanced due diligence.

questions.q: Match each term to its meaning
questions.explain: These four terms make up most AML conversations. The FIU sits within the Central Bank of Sri Lanka.

questions.q: Put the steps for onboarding a new customer in the right order
questions.explain: Verification and screening always come before the account goes live — never open first and check later.
items: Open the account and hand over the welcome kit
Verify identity and screen against sanctions lists
Assess risk and record in the system

questions.q: Which of these customers needs Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD)?
questions.explain: High-risk profiles — like PEPs moving large sums — need EDD: source of funds, senior approval and closer monitoring.
options: A salaried teacher opening a savings account
A foreign PEP opening a high-value investment account
A student opening a basic account

questions.q: Where do banks in Sri Lanka send Suspicious Transaction Reports?
questions.explain: STRs go to the Financial Intelligence Unit, which analyses them and works with law enforcement.

g-cyber.desc: Could you spot a scam before it spots you?
g-cyber.title: Cyber Shield

questions.q: Someone calls saying they're from the bank's IT team and asks for your system password to 'fix an error'. What do you do?
questions.explain: Real IT staff never need your password. This is a vishing attempt — report it so others get warned.
options: Give it — IT needs it to help
Refuse, end the call and report it to IT security

questions.q: The bank may ask a customer to read out their OTP over the phone to verify who they are.
questions.explain: Never. An OTP is for the customer alone. Anyone asking for one is a fraudster — tell customers this every time.

questions.q: Which email is most likely phishing?
questions.explain: Urgency plus a look-alike domain are the two classic phishing tells. Check the sender and never click links you didn't expect.
options: An HR newsletter from your usual internal address
'URGENT: verify your account in 2 hours' from harbor-secure-login.co
A calendar invite from your manager
A system alert that doesn't ask you to click anything

questions.q: Match each scam to how it reaches you
questions.explain: Same trick, different channel — the fraudster wants your credentials, OTP or money.

questions.q: Which password is strongest?
questions.explain: Long passphrases of unrelated words, with a number and symbol, beat short 'complex' passwords that are easy to guess.

questions.q: Leaving your workstation unlocked for 'just two minutes' inside the branch is fine.
questions.explain: Lock it every time (Windows + L). Two minutes is enough for someone to misuse your access — and it'd be logged under your ID.

questions.q: You clicked a suspicious link on your work PC. What should you do FIRST?
questions.explain: Speed matters. Isolate the machine and report immediately so IT can contain any damage.
options: Disconnect from the network and report to IT security right away
Delete the email and forget it

g-daily-2026-09-23.desc: Three quick ones before your first customer.
g-daily-2026-09-23.title: Daily 3 · Scam Watch

questions.q: A customer got an SMS with a link to 'unlock' their blocked card. What do you tell them?
questions.explain: Links in unexpected SMS messages are the most common card-fraud trap. Always direct customers to official channels.
options: Click it quickly before it expires
Don't click — the bank never sends links like that; call our official hotline
Call the number given in the SMS
Forward it to family to check

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a primary identity document for opening an account?
questions.explain: A utility bill can confirm an address, but it doesn't prove who someone is.

questions.q: Withdrawing a fixed deposit before maturity can mean earning a lower interest rate than agreed.
questions.explain: Yes. Premature withdrawal usually carries a reduced rate — explain this before the customer signs.

questions.q: A customer asks something you don't know the answer to. Best response?
questions.explain: Owning the question and following up builds trust far more than a guess.
options: Guess so they aren't kept waiting
Tell them you'll find out, and check with the right person

questions.q: You can share your system login with a colleague covering your desk if your manager is busy.
questions.explain: Never share credentials. Every action is logged under your ID.

questions.q: When handing cash to a customer, you should…
questions.explain: Counting in front of the customer prevents disputes and protects you.
options: Count it out clearly in front of them
Count it quickly in the back office
Let them count it at home
Give it in a sealed envelope without counting

g-digital.desc: CEFTS, SLIPS, LankaQR — know your payment rails.
g-digital.title: Digital Banking Blitz

questions.q: What does CEFTS let customers do?
questions.explain: CEFTS (Common Electronic Fund Transfer Switch), run by LankaPay, moves money between banks in real time, any time.

questions.q: What is LankaQR?
questions.explain: LankaQR lets customers pay any participating merchant by scanning one common QR code from their banking app.
options: Sri Lanka's national QR code payment standard

questions.q: Match each system to what it does
questions.explain: Knowing which rail does what helps you pick the right option for each customer.

questions.q: A CRIB report shows a borrower's credit history across lending institutions in Sri Lanka.
questions.explain: Yes. Lenders report to the Credit Information Bureau, so CRIB gives a picture of a borrower's facilities and repayment record.

questions.q: A customer reports their debit card stolen. Put your steps in order
questions.explain: Identify the customer, then block fast — every minute counts. Disputes and replacement come after the card is safe.
items: Review recent transactions with the customer
Log a dispute for any unauthorised transactions

questions.q: A customer wants their salary and bill payments on their phone, without visiting the branch. Best move?
questions.explain: Onboarding them there and then — and doing the first transaction together — is what makes digital adoption stick.
options: Tell them to come in every month
Help them sign up for digital banking and make a first payment together

questions.q: Who issues Sri Lanka's currency notes?
questions.explain: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka is the sole issuer of currency notes and coins.
options: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka

g-service.desc: Turn tricky moments into loyal customers.
g-service.title: Service Stars

questions.q: An upset customer complains about a long queue. What's your best first response?
questions.explain: People calm down when they feel heard. Acknowledge first, then fix what you can.
options: Listen, acknowledge and apologise for the wait
Ask them to come back later
Direct them to the manager straight away

questions.q: To keep a customer happy, it's okay to promise a loan approval before the credit evaluation is done.
questions.explain: Never promise an outcome you don't control. Set clear expectations on steps and timelines instead.

questions.q: Put the complaint-handling steps in order
questions.explain: Logging every complaint — even resolved ones — helps the bank fix root causes.

questions.q: A customer says a caller from 'the bank' asked for their OTP to reverse a charge. What do you tell them?
questions.explain: An OTP is the customer's final lock. Genuine bank staff never ask for it, on any channel.
options: Share it only if the caller knows your name
Never share an OTP — the bank will never ask for it
Share it if the call came from a local number
Share half of it so they can verify

questions.q: Writing the CVV on a sticky note inside the wallet is fine as long as the card is kept safe.
questions.explain: Anyone holding the wallet then has everything needed for online purchases. The CVV should never be written down.

questions.q: A customer reports a lost card. Put the steps in order.
questions.explain: Identity first, then block before anything else — every minute unblocked is risk.
items: Review recent transactions with the customer

questions.q: What is 'skimming'?
questions.explain: Skimmers hide in card slots and keypads. Loose parts or extra layers on a terminal are a warning sign.
options: Copying card data with a hidden device on an ATM or POS
Splitting a bill across two cards
Using a card abroad without telling the bank

g-daily-2026-09-26.title: Daily 5 · Digital Sprint
g-daily-2026-09-26.desc: Five quick ones on safe digital banking.

questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.explain: Length beats complexity. A long passphrase is far harder to crack than a short word with symbols.

questions.q: Customers should log out of mobile banking when they use a shared or borrowed device.
questions.explain: An open session on someone else's phone is an open door to the account.

questions.q: Match each term to its meaning
questions.explain: Knowing the vocabulary helps you explain security to customers in plain words.
right: Fingerprint or face to log in
A second check after your password

questions.q: A customer's app shows a transfer they didn't make. What comes first?
questions.explain: Stop further loss first by blocking access, then log the dispute so it can be investigated.
options: Ask them to wait a few days
Help them block the channel and report it straight away
Tell them to uninstall the app
Advise them to change their SIM card

questions.q: You may install any free app on a bank laptop if it helps you work faster.
questions.explain: Only IT-approved software goes on bank devices. Free tools are a common way malware gets in.

questions.explain: Under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, cash transactions of LKR 1 million or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) are reported to the FIU.
